cards.note: Genesis 49:1 — *And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.* *My child Methosalam, summon all your brethren and all your household and the elders of the people, that I may talk to them and depart, as is planned for me.* (2 Enoch 57:1) A father who knows his time is short gathers the whole household around him to speak before he goes, just as Jacob called his sons to his bed. Enoch's word is sent down through his son in the same way, so that what he has seen is not left unsaid.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 31:28 — *Gather unto me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, that I may speak these words in their ears, and call heaven and earth to record against them.* *My child Methosalam, summon all your brethren and all your household and the elders of the people, that I may talk to them and depart, as is planned for me.* (2 Enoch 57:1) Moses also has the elders brought to him so that his last words are spoken in their hearing. In both places the elders of the people are summoned because what is about to be said is meant to be carried on after the speaker is gone.

Enoch's words, that he may talk to them and depart as is planned for him, sit in the same line.

threads.title: Gather the elders, that I may speak and depart
threads.summary_md:
Enoch, knowing his time has come, asks his son to bring the people together: *My child Methosalam, summon all your brethren and all your household and the elders of the people, that I may talk to them and depart, as is planned for me.* (2 Enoch 57:1) The son does as he is told: *And Methosalam made haste, and summoned his brethren, Regim, Riman, Uchan, Chermion, Gaidad, and all the elders of the people before the face of his father Enoch; and he blessed them, and said to them:* (2 Enoch 57:2)

It ain't new. The fathers of Yashar'el (Israel) did exactly this when their days drew to an end. *And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.* (Genesis 49:1) Moses, for the same purpose, had the elders of the tribes called to him: *Gather unto me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, that I may speak these words in their ears, and call heaven and earth to record against them.* (Deuteronomy 31:28) When his words were done, the people were blessed: *And this is the blessing, wherewith Moses the man of Elohim (God) blessed the children of Yashar'el (Israel) before his death.* (Deuteronomy 33:1)

The apostles knew the same custom. Peter, near the end, wrote: *Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ) hath shewed me.* (2 Peter 1:14)

What stands out in all of these is one pattern the scriptures keep. The one who is about to go gathers the household and the elders, blesses them, and speaks what must be remembered, so that the word does not die with the man who carried it. Enoch's gathering belongs in that line, and the long farewell that follows is spoken in the hearing of the same assembled elders.
